interest: 1940 Shanghai press claims of a Nazi fifth column in Japan and the death of Melville Cox.
overview: This file (894.00N Nazi Activities/1208, August 31, 1940) consists of correspondence from the American Consulate General in Shanghai transmitting an article published in The Shanghai Evening Post and Mercury regarding German 'Fifth Column' activities in Japan. Consul Richard P. Butrick forwards copies of his despatch to both the Department of State and U.S. Ambassador Joseph C. Grew in Tokyo, noting that while the article is written in an exaggerated and light journalistic style, it may contain elements of truth. The enclosed article by foreign writer 'Seiyo-jin' alleges that German Ambassador General Eugen Ott built an extensive covert network in Japan over several years, influenced the installation of Prince Konoe's totalitarian cabinet in alignment with the Japanese Army, and prompted the July 1940 arrests of prominent British nationals—including Reuters correspondent Melville J. Cox—as a fabricated counter-scare to distract from German machinations.
